title: Holistic Design towards Resource-Stringent Binary Vector Symbolic Architecture
problem: Binary Vector Symbolic Architecture offers minimal memory and fast execution but suffers from inferior inference accuracy and designs that prioritize algorithmic performance over hardware efficiency, limiting practical deployment on ultra-lightweight devices.
motivation: Ultra-lightweight embedded classification requires algorithms that simultaneously optimize algorithmic accuracy and hardware implementation efficiency, combining algorithmic and hardware-level innovations.
method: Binary Vector Symbolic Architecture does AI inference with minimal memory, but normally sacrifices accuracy to stay efficient. UniVSA fixes this by redesigning both the algorithm and the hardware at the same time. It uses lightweight modules—small, efficient components—and a specialized design flow that optimizes both together. The result is better accuracy while maintaining a small memory footprint and efficient execution on ultra-lightweight devices.
key_novelty: The key idea is designing the algorithm and hardware together as one integrated system instead of separate pieces, which lets binary Vector Symbolic Architecture achieve better accuracy while staying efficient on tiny devices.
contributions: UniVSA co-optimization framework combining algorithmic and hardware design for binary VSA
Novel lightweight modules and design flow tailored for optimal hardware performance
Surpasses traditional ML methods in resource-limited settings with smaller memory, lower latency
Reduced resource demand and power consumption compared to state-of-the-art binary VSA

metrics.accuracy: Surpasses traditional ML methods on resource-limited devices
metrics.other: Lower latency, reduced resource demand, decreased power consumption

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation focused on ultra-lightweight device benchmarks.
primary_theme: Co-designed algorithm-hardware binary Vector Symbolic Architecture for ultra-lightweight devices
